purpose: Machine-readable PAPER CLAIM -> CODE SYMBOL map for the TransformerPath analytical credibility paper. Every central methodological claim the paper makes is mapped to a real implementation object, test, or runtime path, and classified so any claim WITHOUT an implementation is removed or qualified. Only claims verified against source in this session are listed; nothing is asserted beyond what the code actually does.
generator: read-only audit of viz/viz-math.js, tests/viz-math.test.js, engine/design-core.js, design-engine.js, viz/short-circuit.js

claims.paper_claim: Six-state credibility hierarchy: INSUFFICIENT_DATA -> CALCULATED -> BENCHMARKED -> CRITERION_CHECKED -> PRELIMINARY_ENGINEERING -> ENGINEERING_REVIEWED.
claims.note: The paper MUST use these exact six state names (and the derived machine-readable fields), matching code terminology 1:1. No invented seven/eight-state taxonomy.

claims.implementation: thermalEngine -> SINGLE-AGGREGATE hot-spot + life (one global load/loss)
claims.note: thermalEngine is a single-lump IEC-60076-7-style hot-spot/life model, NOT winding-by-winding (no per-winding current/area/material/duration/criterion). Any 'winding-by-winding thermal verification' claim must be removed or renamed to 'aggregate hot-spot rate/life screening'. It also returns bare state:'CALCULATED' with no acceptance-criterion step.

claims.paper_claim: Connection topology produces materially different winding quantities; sqrt(3) turns relationship.
claims.implementation: vecGroup (clock+phase volt: star V/sqrt(3), delta V_line) ; design-core turns ratio
claims.symbol_or_path: viz/viz-math.js -> vecGroup; engine/design-core.js -> turns_ratio (V_hv/V_lv, ignores vector-group)
claims.note: vecGroup does clock-angle + phase-voltage (star=1/sqrt(3)) only; it does NOT compute ampere-turns balance, zero-sequence (Z0/ZN), or winding currents. design-core turns_ratio ignores vector-group phase shift. So 'topology explicitness' is partial: phase-voltage per connection is implemented, but the full winding-quantity/AT and ZN cases are NOT. The paper must not claim a completed topology case that the code cannot produce.
